newsitem.title: SPAIN: Strike called by Basque rebels fails to bite.
newsitem.headline: Strike called by Basque rebels fails to bite.

text.p: A general strike called by the political wing of separatist rebels ETA in Spain's Basque region failed to bite early on Friday, but residents expected trouble later as pickets appeared.

Dozens of pickets were arrested on Friday morning, Basque government officials said. There were scattered incidents throughout the region as supporters of the strike, called by Herri Batasuna (HB) to protest at the jailing of its leaders, tried to block public transport.
They set fire to a city bus in Bilbao and put up a barricade across train tracks near Vitoria, the region's capital, forcing a temporary halt in service. Some roads were barricaded in San Sebastian.
Police said the doorlocks of several businesses had been clogged with silicone.
Taxis and buses maintained regular service with the help of police escorts and people were able to go to work and school without difficulty, the Basque transport department said.
Businesses in some areas took collective decisions to open on Saturday instead of Friday to avoid pressure from the rebels, but others insisted they would not be blackmailed with violence.
HB sent threatening letters to businesses, schools and workers this week urging them to observe the work stoppage.
The letters sent a shiver of fear through Basque society, which has learned in 29 years of ETA's struggle for independence that the rebels do not make idle threats.
ETA has killed some 800 people, many of them for failing to cooperate with the group.
"We're frightened, but we're going to send our children to school," one woman at a bus stop said. "A normal day is our right and no one is going to take it away."
HB, which is supported by an estimated 10-15 percent of Basques, has planned demonstrations throughout the day.

The last HB demonstration on February 15 deteriorated into a violent clash between thousands of protesters and police who fired live bullets into a crowd and wounded two. Tens more were injured by rubber bullets.
